newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 30.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The mood was positive at the meeting beetween Pds leader Massimo D'Alema and opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, but the vote on the bicameral commission for constitutional reforms has been postponed until January, after the approval of the 1997 budget by parliament (all).

* In an interview Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick says he is going to present a draft law by the end of the year for a political solution to Tangentopoli (Bribesville). "The opposition between politicians and magistrates must come to an end" (Repubblica).
* The government called a new vote of confidence, its second in a week, to try to force through parliament a contested decree over development projects. The vote was set for today.
* A public prosecutor asked for Marcello Dell'Utri, former head of Silvio Berlusconi's Publitalia advertising company, to be sent for trial on charges of criminal association with the mafia (all).
* Michele Tedeschi, head of debt-laden state industrial holding Iri, ruled out the transfer to the Treasury of assets that could be privatised as a way of cutting its borrowing (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi presented to the European Commission three proposals to cover 1996 expected losses at state holding company IRI of three trillion lire. One of these includes the transfer to the Treasury of Iri's holding Gepi, valued at 2.6 trillion lire (all).

* The Upper House commission for Public Works has decided to suspend discussions over the draft law for the creation of a telecom regulating Authority, which is a prerequisite for the privatisation of state telecom holding Stet. The Freedom alliance had presented 6,000 amendments against the project (all).

* Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo said it would launch a rescue plan for two southern Italian savings banks which it controls. The plan for Caripuglia and Carical would involve an 800 billion lire capital increase (all).
* Eni dominated trade at the Milan stock exchange two days after its second-tranche sale and closed 0.61 percent higher at 7,234 lire (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
